changes.current_line: Financial infrastructure to grow globally, in every currency.
changes.change: Stop running in-house sitter payouts every time you launch a new country: pay sitters locally, in their currency, from one platform.
changes.why: Fetchwell's buying case was the cost of keeping its own payout code alive across new countries, not growth in the abstract.

changes.current_line: Customers see an average uplift in authorization rates with Authorization Boost and Adaptive Acceptance.
changes.change: For sitter-economics and marketplace buyers, stop leading with average authorization-rate uplift; lead with docs, the sandbox, and payouts in their own numbers.
changes.why: Daniel dismissed the generic average uplift against his own $38 average booking, and the pitch drew silence.

changes.current_line: Built for developers: launch payments fast with our APIs, docs and sandbox.
changes.change: Build a working payout flow over a weekend with our docs and sandbox, for platforms paying out sitters, drivers or sellers.
changes.why: The docs and sandbox drew the only strong reaction, and a customer engineer built a working payout flow on them over a weekend.

changes.change: A written answer for PayPal, Venmo and saved-card handling during migration, with a named account owner and a reference customer of similar scale.
changes.why: Loss-avoidance is the opening a competitor can use, and the PayPal, Venmo and saved-card questions remain open with no written answer.
